dimension: Job evaluation factor: Communication and relationship skills
statement: Skills needed to communicate with, and build relationships with, colleagues, patients, the public, and partners. Considers how complex, sensitive, or contentious the information is, and any barriers to understanding or acceptance.
expected_level_description: Reference level 5: Gives highly complex or contentious information needing developed persuasion and negotiation, presents to large groups, or communicates where there are significant barriers to acceptance. Levels: 1: Gives and receives routine information orally, mainly with colleagues. | 2: Gives and receives routine information orally, in writing, or electronically, with colleagues and others. | 3: Gives routine information needing tact or persuasion, or complex or sensitive information, or straightforward training to groups. | 4: Gives complex, sensitive, or contentious information needing persuasion, negotiation, or training skills, or highly complex information. | 5: Gives highly complex or contentious information needing developed persuasion and negotiation, presents to large groups, or communicates where there are significant barriers to acceptance. | 6: Gives highly complex, highly contentious information where there are significant barriers to acceptance, using the highest level of communication skills.

dimension: Job evaluation factor: Knowledge, training, and experience
statement: The knowledge and experience needed to do the job, from any source, including formal training, qualifications, and experience.
expected_level_description: Reference level 7: Highly developed specialist knowledge across the range of the specialism (master's level or equivalent). Levels: 1: A few routine procedures, learned on the job in a short induction. | 2: A range of routine procedures, learned through on-the-job training and induction. | 3: A range of procedures, some non-routine, needing base-level theory (for example a level 3 qualification or equivalent experience). | 4: A range of procedures, mostly non-routine, needing intermediate theory (for example a foundation degree or equivalent experience). | 5: Expertise in a specialism, underpinned by theory or practical experience (degree level or equivalent). | 6: Specialist knowledge across the range of the specialism (postgraduate diploma level or equivalent). | 7: Highly developed specialist knowledge across the range of the specialism (master's level or equivalent). | 8: Advanced knowledge (doctorate plus further training or equivalent), or specialist knowledge across more than one discipline built over a long period.

dimension: Job evaluation factor: Analytical and judgemental skills
statement: The analysis and judgement needed to process information, solve problems, and make decisions.
expected_level_description: Reference level 4: Judgements on complex facts or situations needing analysis, interpretation, and comparison of options. Levels: 1: Judgements on straightforward facts or situations. | 2: Judgements on facts or situations, some needing analysis. | 3: Judgements on a range of facts or situations needing analysis or comparison of options. | 4: Judgements on complex facts or situations needing analysis, interpretation, and comparison of options. | 5: Judgements on highly complex facts or situations needing analysis, interpretation, and comparison of options.

dimension: Job evaluation factor: Planning and organisational skills
statement: The planning and organising needed to run activities, programmes, services, or strategies.
expected_level_description: Reference level 4: Plans a broad range of complex activities or strategies, adjusting them as needed. Levels: 1: Organises own day-to-day work. | 2: Plans straightforward tasks or activities, some ongoing. | 3: Plans several complex activities, adjusting plans as needed. | 4: Plans a broad range of complex activities or strategies, adjusting them as needed. | 5: Forms long-term strategic plans, with uncertainty and effects across the organisation.

dimension: Job evaluation factor: Physical skills
statement: The physical skills needed, such as dexterity, coordination, keyboard skills, and driving.
expected_level_description: Reference level 2: Skills gained through practice, such as standard keyboard use or driving. Levels: 1: Little need for physical skills. | 2: Skills gained through practice, such as standard keyboard use or driving. | 3: Developed skills needing speed or accuracy, such as advanced keyboard use. | 4: Highly developed skills needing precision or speed and high hand–eye coordination. | 5: The highest level of precision, speed, and coordination.

dimension: Job evaluation factor: Responsibility for patient and client care
statement: Responsibility for assessing, treating, caring for, or advising patients and clients. For most digital and corporate roles this is incidental contact only.
expected_level_description: Reference level 1: Helps patients, clients, or relatives during incidental contact. Levels: 1: Helps patients, clients, or relatives during incidental contact. | 2: Gives general non-clinical advice, information, or services directly to patients or the public. | 3: Gives personal care, basic clinical technical services, or basic clinical advice. | 4: Carries out clinical care, provides clinical technical services, or advises on the care of patients. | 5: Develops programmes of care, provides specialist clinical technical services, or gives specialised advice on patient care. | 6: Develops specialised care, gives highly specialised advice, or is accountable for part of a clinical service. | 7: Accountable for delivering a clinical or care service. | 8: Corporate responsibility for clinical or care services.

dimension: Job evaluation factor: Responsibility for policy and service development
statement: Responsibility for developing and implementing policies and services, and how far the effects reach.
expected_level_description: Reference level 3: Implements policies for own area and proposes changes that affect other areas. Levels: 1: Follows policies set by others; may comment on changes. | 2: Implements policies for own area and proposes changes to its practices. | 3: Implements policies for own area and proposes changes that affect other areas. | 4: Implements policy and develops policy or services for a service or several areas. | 5: Implements and develops a range of policies or services for a directorate. | 6: Corporate responsibility for major policy or service development across or beyond the organisation.

dimension: Job evaluation factor: Responsibility for financial and physical resources
statement: Responsibility for money, budgets, equipment, stock, buildings, and other assets.
expected_level_description: Reference level 2: Handles cash or valuables, looks after equipment used by others, controls stock, or authorises small payments. Levels: 1: Takes personal care of equipment and resources used in own work. | 2: Handles cash or valuables, looks after equipment used by others, controls stock, or authorises small payments. | 3: Authorises payments, buys some assets or supplies, monitors or holds a delegated budget, or maintains assets. | 4: Holds or sets the budget for a department or service, or buys or maintains its assets. | 5: Holds or sets budgets, or manages assets, for several services. | 6: Corporate responsibility for the organisation's finances or assets.

dimension: Job evaluation factor: Responsibility for people
statement: Responsibility for managing, supervising, training, or developing staff, or for providing people (HR) services.
expected_level_description: Reference level 3: Manages a group of staff day to day, teaches core or specialist training, or gives core HR advice. Levels: 1: Shows own work routines to new or less experienced colleagues. | 2: Supervises or coordinates staff day to day, trains others regularly, or gives basic HR advice. | 3: Manages a group of staff day to day, teaches core or specialist training, or gives core HR advice. | 4: Line manages a function or department, designs training programmes as a main duty, or delivers a full range of HR services. | 5: Line manages several departments, or manages training or a large part of HR across the organisation. | 6: Corporate responsibility for the organisation's people or HR function.

dimension: Job evaluation factor: Responsibility for information resources
statement: Responsibility for information and information systems, paper or digital, including records, data, and the systems that hold them.
expected_level_description: Reference level 4: Adapts or designs information systems to others' specifications, or runs information systems for a department as the main duty. Levels: 1: Records information that the job holder produces. | 2: Enters or stores data compiled by others, or occasionally writes reports or queries. | 3: Takes formal minutes, regularly writes reports or queries, or maintains information systems as a significant duty. | 4: Adapts or designs information systems to others' specifications, or runs information systems for a department as the main duty. | 5: Designs and develops major information systems, or runs information systems for several services as the main duty. | 6: Manages and develops information systems across the organisation as the main duty. | 7: Corporate responsibility for the organisation's information systems.

dimension: Job evaluation factor: Responsibility for research and development
statement: Responsibility for formal research, development, evaluation, audits, testing, and trials.
expected_level_description: Reference level 2: Regularly does research, development, trials, or equipment and system testing as part of the job. Levels: 1: Carries out surveys or audits for own work; occasionally takes part in research or testing. | 2: Regularly does research, development, trials, or equipment and system testing as part of the job. | 3: Carries out research or development within formal programmes as a main duty. | 4: Coordinates and carries out research and development programmes. | 5: Initiates and develops research and development programmes that support the organisation's objectives. | 6: Initiates and develops research and development programmes with effects beyond the organisation.

dimension: Job evaluation factor: Freedom to act
statement: How far the job holder decides what to do and how, and how closely their work is supervised.
expected_level_description: Reference level 4: Results are defined, but the job holder decides how to achieve them, within broad policy. Levels: 1: Works within set procedures, with supervision close by. | 2: Follows standard procedures and precedent; someone is usually available to ask; work may be checked. | 3: Follows defined policies and procedures; work is managed rather than supervised. | 4: Results are defined, but the job holder decides how to achieve them, within broad policy. | 5: Works within general policies, and in most cases decides how to interpret them. | 6: Interprets overall policy and strategy to set goals and standards.

dimension: Job evaluation factor: Physical effort
statement: The physical effort needed, considering its frequency, duration, and intensity.
expected_level_description: Reference level 1: Sitting, standing, and walking, with little physical effort. Levels: 1: Sitting, standing, and walking, with little physical effort. | 2: Frequent sitting or standing in a restricted position, or occasional light to moderate effort. | 3: Frequent light effort for long periods, or frequent moderate effort for short periods. | 4: Ongoing light effort, frequent moderate effort for long periods, or occasional intense effort. | 5: Ongoing moderate effort, or frequent intense effort.

dimension: Job evaluation factor: Mental effort
statement: The concentration needed, considering its frequency, duration, and how predictable the work is.
expected_level_description: Reference level 4: Frequent prolonged concentration, or occasional intense concentration. Levels: 1: General attention; occasional concentration on predictable work. | 2: Frequent concentration on predictable work, or occasional concentration on unpredictable work. | 3: Frequent concentration on unpredictable work, or occasional prolonged concentration. | 4: Frequent prolonged concentration, or occasional intense concentration. | 5: Frequent intense concentration.

dimension: Job evaluation factor: Emotional effort
statement: The emotional demands of the job, from direct or indirect exposure to distressing circumstances, such as reading distressing case records or handling serious incidents.
expected_level_description: Reference level 1: Rare exposure, or occasional indirect exposure, to distressing circumstances. Levels: 1: Rare exposure, or occasional indirect exposure, to distressing circumstances. | 2: Occasional exposure, or frequent indirect exposure, to distressing circumstances. | 3: Frequent exposure to distressing circumstances, or occasional exposure to highly distressing ones. | 4: Occasional exposure to traumatic circumstances, or frequent exposure to highly distressing ones.

dimension: Job evaluation factor: Working conditions
statement: Exposure to unpleasant conditions or hazards. Near-continuous screen use on most days counts at level 2.
expected_level_description: Reference level 2: Occasional unpleasant conditions, frequent travel or outdoor work, or near-continuous screen use on most days. Levels: 1: Rare exposure to unpleasant conditions. | 2: Occasional unpleasant conditions, frequent travel or outdoor work, or near-continuous screen use on most days. | 3: Frequent unpleasant conditions, or occasional highly unpleasant ones. | 4: Some exposure to hazards, or frequent highly unpleasant conditions. | 5: Considerable exposure to hazards.

dimension: Skill: Communicating between the technical and non-technical
statement: Communicating between the technical and non-technical involves conveying information using the most effective medium and language for the audience.
expected_level_description: You can: - mediate between people and strengthen relationships, adopting the appropriate communication method with stakeholders at all levels - manage stakeholder expectations and moderate difficult discussions about high risk and complex topics, even within constrained timescales - speak on behalf of, and represent the community to, large audiences inside and outside the organisation
rating_scale: 0 Not yet | 1 Awareness | 2 Working | 3 Practitioner | 4 Expert

dimension: Skill: Designing and executing tests
statement: Designing and executing tests involves applying appropriate test types and techniques to create and run tests that align to user needs and requirements.
expected_level_description: You can: - set up suitable environments - influence and guide the use of appropriate test types and techniques to mitigate risk early - lead others in designing, building, maintaining and executing tests that align to user needs and requirements - contribute to developing and implementing standards for designing and executing tests - improve test types and techniques through a structured process.
next_level_description: Expert: You can: - set standards and influence organisational decisions for test types, techniques, design and execution - coach others in test types, techniques, design and execution - advocate for continuous improvement and refinement of test types and techniques - make strategic decisions on new or improved test types and techniques used in your area
rating_scale: 0 Not yet | 1 Awareness | 2 Working | 3 Practitioner | 4 Expert

dimension: Skill: Managing, reporting and resolving defects
statement: Managing, reporting and resolving defects involves reporting progress, outcomes and issues, whilst contributing to improving defect management processes.
expected_level_description: You can: - lead and coach others in improving test and defect management processes - support others in assessing complex and challenging defects across the organisation - lead and coach others in using defect patterns and trends to make tactical and strategic recommendations - influence improvements to quality processes, informed by defect patterns and trends
rating_scale: 0 Not yet | 1 Awareness | 2 Working | 3 Practitioner | 4 Expert

dimension: Skill: Test analysis
statement: Test analysis involves analysing information, such as requirements, user stories, designs and specifications, to identify and understand how to act on quality risks.
expected_level_description: You can: - lead work with stakeholders across teams to determine which functional and non-functional quality characteristics add value - determine if an approach needs to change based on effort and risk - ensure test needs are implemented early - use multiple techniques to analyse complex information to identify risks - coach others in test analysis
next_level_description: Expert: You can: - lead and guide multiple teams in test analysis, ensuring it is implemented early in the life cycle - advocate for risk-based analysis to drive improvements across many teams - set standards and principles for test analysis across the organisation
rating_scale: 0 Not yet | 1 Awareness | 2 Working | 3 Practitioner | 4 Expert

dimension: Skill: Test and quality planning
statement: Test and quality planning involves creating, following and adapting quality testing activities to ensure the quality of products, services and programmes.
expected_level_description: You can: - create and manage multiple quality testing plans, approaches and strategies - lead and guide multiple teams in adopting quality testing strategy - advocate for early quality testing involvement in organisational delivery processes - guide teams across an organisation in optimising quality testing approaches, plans and strategies by using appropriate data
rating_scale: 0 Not yet | 1 Awareness | 2 Working | 3 Practitioner | 4 Expert

dimension: Skill: Test engineering

expected_level_description: You can: - explain why testing processes, environments and tools are important - follow test engineering practices and standards, with support - support the maintenance of automated tests and tools required for testing
next_level_description: Working: You can: - use test engineering frameworks and tools to support testing activities - follow test engineering practices and standards, such as source control and continuous integration, continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines - integrate and execute tests to ensure early testing and continuous feedback - create and maintain automated tests, with some support - write and review coded solutions, with some support
rating_scale: 0 Not yet | 1 Awareness | 2 Working | 3 Practitioner | 4 Expert

dimension: Skill: Understanding health and care services

expected_level_description: You can: - analyse how a service fits into care pathways across organisations - work with clinicians, care staff, and patients to shape digital services - explain the effect of digital decisions on care, safety, and staff workload
next_level_description: Expert: You can: - shape organisational strategy using a deep understanding of the health and care system - represent the organisation with health and care partners and leaders - anticipate how policy and service changes will affect digital services and care

next_level_description: Expert: You can: - own the clinical risk management system for the organisation - set clinical safety policy and assure safety cases for major systems - lead the response to serious safety incidents involving health IT - build a culture of clinical safety across digital teams

next_level_description: Practitioner: You can: - lead data protection impact assessments and information sharing agreements - advise teams on lawful basis, consent, confidentiality, and retention - investigate incidents and recommend improvements
